name: Magic Answer Orb
description: Murmur, a smoky glass vessel for uncertain things. Shake the liquid, wait for a thought to surface, and ask again in four original voices.

assets.credit: Original Murmur glass vessel, plaque and optical rendering

compatibility: Canvas 2D, Pointer Events, ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver and CSS container queries. Web Audio is optional, with no AudioContext created until a deliberate Sound action.
Mouse, captured touch, pen and keyboard. The answer is repeated as accessible HTML at a comfortable reading size, with announcements when it has finished surfacing.
Reduced motion resolves a shake immediately. Hidden tabs, offscreen previews and pause suspend the motion and automatic-shake countdown. Pausing silences current voices.
One canvas, 80 suspended grains and a cached answer texture. Backing width caps at 1600 px. All observer, event, texture, audio and animation resources are cleaned up on disposal.
notes: Murmur is an original smoky colored-glass orb with a bronze rest and a faceted pale answer plaque. It uses no commercial toy branding, numbered black-and-white shell, copied answer artwork, recordings or fonts.

Four original collections contain 48 answers: yes/no/perhaps, poetic, absurd and creative prompts. Seeded shuffle bags visit every answer once per cycle, with no immediate repeat, and keep a separate position for each set.

Tap or press Space/Enter to shake. Dragging distance, speed and reversals produce a bounded energy value that changes the orb motion and liquid currents. A new shake can interrupt an unfinished reveal.

The hidden plaque rotates and rises through a drawn liquid volume, followed by damped settling. This is a layered Canvas optical illustration, not a volumetric fluid simulation. The answer is selected at shake time but enters the notebook only after the reveal completes.

Questions do not affect answer selection or leave the browser. The last six completed answers and questions live in this tab only. Notebook JSON is an explicit download; PNG prints capture the vessel and answer without the question. Shared presets and source exports contain only settings.

Five presets, optical and sequence controls, optional synthesized sound, automatic shaking and ordinary HTML answer controls are included. Auto-shake waits until the current reveal has completed, then counts the chosen interval.
reuse: AnswerEngine in answers.js is independent of animation and DOM. Supply named answer collections and a seed; next(mode), snapshot() and restore() provide a reproducible sequence.

OrbMotion and poseAt define the reveal separately from the renderer. createAnswerOrb(canvas, settings, hooks) combines these, accepts custom answer sets, and reports shake, phase and completed-answer events.

The standalone source export contains the original illustration, audio engine, full studio, five presets and a neutral integration with custom onboarding prompts. No Tampa runtime or external assets are needed.
